schemaVersion.description:
Wire-IR schema version: pinned literal `1.0`. While the Contracts package
is pre-1.0 a minor may narrow this document in place and every narrowing
must be listed in `schemas/breaking-changes.allowlist.json`; after 1.0 a
breaking change requires a V2 root.

name.description: Workflow name (the IR identity, matches the builder's `WorkflowDefinition.Name`).

gates.description:
Gate declarations for this workflow (#150, DR-3). Consumer-plane data: the
generated saga does NOT consume gates — they flow through the shared wire IR
so both runtimes see the same gate vocabulary from birth. OPTIONAL and
additive; a workflow with no declared gates omits the slot entirely.

A GateStep may back-reference a declaration here by its `gateId`. That a
`gateId` must name an id present in this list is a semantic rule JSON Schema
cannot express (see README, "Dangling gateId"); the build-time import
front-end enforces it (DR-13/DR-15), not this schema.

diagnosticForks.description:
Diagnostic fork edges for this workflow (#151, DR-10). The DECLARATIVE half of
the fork/compensation edge (DR-7): where the workflow may fork, the closed
triggers permitted with their evidence-ref schema, the `maxForks` bound, and
the compensation seed. OPTIONAL and additive — a workflow with no fork edge
omits the slot entirely, so this is a NON-BREAKING wire change.

INV-8: every reference inside a DiagnosticForkDefinition is a string moniker,
never a CLR type. The generated saga lowers the edge (DR-9); the runtime
companion is ForkOccurrence (DR-8) in the Events family.

contentHash.description:
SHA-256 over this definition's STRUCTURAL fields, lowercase hex (#193
kernel `identity.contentHash`). Prose is excluded, on the same rules
`OntologyGraphHasher` already applies: documentation churn must not change
the hash, because the hash exists to say when the shape changed.

OPTIONAL and additive. A producer that does not stamp one omits the slot,
and no Strategos path requires it. #204 reads it for tamper and skew
detection across an assembly boundary.

authority.description:
The #193 kernel's authority frame — invariants, goals, assumptions,
delegated decisions and escalation boundaries (#193, DR-kernel).

**Carried, not proved in 3.0.** Strategos serializes this block and checks
none of it. See `WorkflowAuthorityV1`.

entryStepId.description: Step id of the workflow entry step, if set.

terminalStepId.description: Step id of the workflow terminal step, if set.

description:
Wire-IR root for a serialized Strategos workflow (issue #50).

This is the **wire contract** — the flat, language-neutral document that
cross-product consumers (Exarchos Zod, Basileus, visualization, schema diff)
read. It is the export-only projection target of the in-memory builder IR
`WorkflowDefinition<TState>` (see `WorkflowDefinitionProjection.ToContract`):
the projection drops executable code (LB-1) and reduces CLR `System.Type`
handles to simple-name string monikers (LB-2).

`schemaVersion` is a pinned literal `1.0`. While the Contracts package is
pre-1.0 a minor may narrow this document in place, and every narrowing must
be listed in `schemas/breaking-changes.allowlist.json`; after 1.0 a breaking
change requires a V2 root.

ActionAllPredicateV1.description: Conjunction. Empty input canonicalizes to true in the runtime model.

ActionAnyPredicateV1.description: Disjunction. Empty input canonicalizes to false in the runtime model.

ActionComparisonOperatorV1.description: The comparison operators accepted by the closed action-predicate language.

ActionCustomPredicateV1.description:
An explicitly opaque predicate evaluated by a stable registered key.
Description text is deliberately absent: it is presentation metadata on the
surrounding requirement or guarantee and is not part of semantic identity.

ActionDecimalLiteralV1.description: An exact decimal encoded as a canonical base-10 string without exponent notation.

ActionEnumLiteralV1.description: A member of a named ontology enum.

ActionEventResourceV1.description: An event resource declared in a custom predicate's read set.

ActionExternalResourceV1.description: An external resource declared in a custom predicate's read set.

ActionFalsePredicateV1.description: Predicate that is satisfied by no state.

expression.description: Canonical display projection; consumers never parse this field.

ActionGuaranteeV1.description: One typed post-state guarantee carried in schema metadata.

ActionIntegerLiteralV1.description:
An arbitrary-precision integer encoded as a canonical base-10 string.
JSON numbers are deliberately excluded because their precision is transport dependent.

ActionLinkExistsPredicateV1.description: Assert that a named ontology link is present.

ActionLinkPathSegmentV1.description: A non-empty segment in an ontology relation traversal path.

ActionLinkResourceV1.description: A link resource declared in a custom predicate's read set.

ActionLiteralV1.description:
Version 1 of the closed literal vocabulary used by action predicates.
Floating-point values are intentionally not part of this union.

ActionNullLiteralV1.description: An explicit null literal. Missing data is not represented by this arm.

ActionPredicateScalarKindV1.description: The scalar domain of a property compared by an action predicate.

ActionPredicateV1.description:
Version 1 of the immutable, closed action-predicate language. Unknown kinds
are invalid; consumers must never reinterpret them as custom or true.

ActionPropertyComparisonPredicateV1.description: Compare one ontology property with a typed literal.

enumTypeName.description: Required for enum properties; absent for every other scalar kind.

ActionPropertyReferenceV1.description: Compare one ontology property with a typed literal.

ActionPropertyResourceV1.description: A property resource declared in a custom predicate's read set.

ActionReferenceV1.description:
Language-neutral identity of an ontology action performed by a workflow step
occurrence. Every component is a name; no runtime or CLR type identity crosses
the wire boundary.

ActionRelationHoldsPredicateV1.description: Assert that a named relation holds after following an ontology link path.

ActionResourceV1.description: Closed resource vocabulary for a custom predicate's declared read set.

ActionSymbolLiteralV1.description: A symbolic identifier whose identity is its ordinal token.

ActionTruePredicateV1.description: Predicate that is satisfied by every state.

precedingStepId.description: Step id immediately preceding this approval gate.

hasContext.description:
Declares this approval carried context configuration (a static message or a
runtime context factory) whose body is dropped from the wire — the
declarative-only lossiness marker for approvals (DR-14), mirroring the
delegate step's lambda marker. Present and true only when context was
configured; omitted for a context-free approval point.

ApprovalDefinition.description:
Wire-IR approval point — a human-approval pause (mirrors the builder's
`ApprovalDefinition`). The approver CLR type reduces to a simple-name moniker
(LB-2); the approval configuration's context body (a static message or a
runtime context factory, a CLR expression) is intentionally **not** carried
on the wire (declarative-only, LB-1), but its presence is marked by
`hasContext` so the loss is visible in the data rather than silent (DR-14).

nestedApprovals.description: Nested approval gates within the escalation, if any.

ApprovalEscalationDefinition.description:
Wire-IR approval-escalation handler — steps run when an approval escalates
(mirrors the builder's `ApprovalEscalationDefinition`).

ApprovalRejectionDefinition.description:
Wire-IR approval-rejection handler — steps run when an approval is rejected
(mirrors the builder's `ApprovalRejectionDefinition`).

ApprovalStep.description:
Approval step — a human-approval pause point. `approverType` is the simple-name
moniker of the approver CLR type (LB-2).

level.description: The required level on that axis.

AuthorityCoordinateV1.description:
Wire projection of the authority product lattice (#165, #193 kernel).

The lattice itself is CLR-only today — the `AuthorityLattice` type under
`Strategos.Ontology.Descriptors`, with its axes, descriptors and
requirement. Only the `x-strategos-authority` NAME string crosses the wire
today, so a consumer that
receives an action contract cannot tell whether one authority dominates
another. These models carry the lattice itself, so the dominance test is
decidable on the wire.

Declarative-only (LB-1) and moniker-only (LB-2, INV-8): every member is a
string or a string map. No CLR `Type` handle is projected.One axis-to-level pair.

A coordinate is an ORDERED ARRAY of these pairs rather than a map, for one
reason: `contentHash` must be deterministic. A JSON object has no canonical
member order, so two producers serializing the same coordinate can emit two
byte sequences and therefore two digests. An array sorted ordinally by `axis`
has exactly one serialization. `OntologyGraphHasher` already sorts every
collection before hashing for the same reason.

coordinates.description: The strongest required level on each axis, ordered ordinally by `axis`.

sourceAuthorities.description:
The authority literals whose join produced this coordinate. Provenance
only — the coordinate above is the semantic identity.

AuthorityRequirementV1.description:
The pointwise join of one or more named authorities — what an action or a
workflow step REQUIRES. Mirrors `AuthorityRequirement`.

This is the wire form of the kernel's `tasks[].capabilities[]`. It is a
coordinate, not a name list, so a consumer can compare two requirements
without resolving either against a lattice.

approval.description: Optional approval gate guarding this path.

BranchPointDefinition.description:

requiredOnFailure.description:

timeout.description:

lambda.description: Declares this step was a lambda whose body was dropped (LB-1). Always true.

DelegateStep.description:
Delegate (lambda) step — built via `StepDefinition.CreateFromLambda` (LB-1).
The wire contract **never carries executable code**: the `Delegate` body is
dropped and its loss made visible by the `lambda: true` marker. There is no
field on this arm that can hold a delegate or executable.

anchorStepIds.description:
The anchor step monikers — the step ids where this workflow may fork (INV-8:
simple-name step id monikers, never CLR types). At least one anchor: a fork
edge with nowhere to fork is unrepresentable.

permittedTriggers.description:
The closed triggers permitted to fork this workflow, each paired with its
declaration-side evidence-ref schema (PermittedForkTrigger). At least one:
the edge is inexpressible without declaring a permitted trigger (DR-7).

maxForks.description:
Upper bound on the forks this edge may spawn. The generated guard enforces it
(DR-9; the LoopDefinition.maxIterations forced-exit precedent) — exceeding it
routes to a blocked / human-escalation terminal. At least 1: a bound of 0
forbids the very fork the edge exists to permit.

compensationSeed.description:
The compensation seed moniker (INV-8: a plain string moniker, never a CLR
type) — the seed the fork routes compensation to, composing with the existing
Compensate / OnFailure merged trigger site (DR-9). REQUIRED and non-empty.

DiagnosticForkDefinition.description:
Wire-IR diagnostic fork edge (#151, DR-10 → #100): the DECLARATIVE half of the
basileus #394 rollback-and-fork verb, and the shared combinator exarchos #1258
lowers to. Names WHERE a workflow may fork (anchor step monikers), WHICH closed
triggers may fork it paired with the evidence fields each requires
(PermittedForkTrigger — the declaration side), a `maxForks` upper bound the
generated guard enforces (DR-9; the LoopDefinition.maxIterations forced-exit
precedent), and the compensation seed the fork routes to.

INV-8: EVERY step/type reference on this shape is a string moniker — the anchor
step ids, the evidence field names, and the compensation seed are all plain
strings; the only typed reference is the closed ForkTrigger enum (a snake_case
wire vocabulary, not a CLR type). Nothing here carries a runtime `Type`, an
assembly-qualified name, or executable code.

OPTIONAL and additive on WorkflowDefinitionV1 (the `diagnosticForks?` slot): a
workflow that declares no fork edge omits the slot entirely, so introducing it
is a NON-BREAKING wire change. The generated saga lowers it (DR-9); the
runtime-occurrence companion is ForkOccurrence (DR-8), in the Events family.

triggerStepId.description: Step id that triggers this handler, if step-scoped.

isTerminal.description: Whether the handler terminates the workflow.

FailureHandlerDefinition.description:
Wire-IR failure handler — scoped recovery steps (mirrors the builder's
`FailureHandlerDefinition`).

FailureHandlerScope.description:
Scope of a failure handler (mirrors the builder's `FailureHandlerScope`):
the whole workflow, a single step, or one fork path.

pathIndex.description: Zero-based path index within the fork.

steps.description: Steps executed on this concurrent path.

ForkPathDefinition.description:
Wire-IR fork path — one concurrent branch of a fork (mirrors the builder's
`ForkPathDefinition`).

fromStepId.description: Step id where the fork originates.

joinStepId.description: Step id where the concurrent paths rejoin.

ForkPointDefinition.description:
Wire-IR fork point — a fan-out into concurrent paths that rejoin at a join
step (mirrors the builder's `ForkPointDefinition`).

ForkTrigger.description:
Closed enum of the TRIGGERS that may fork a workflow's diagnostic path
(#151, DR-8) — the declaration-side trigger vocabulary shared across the
contract boundary so both runtimes fork on ONE trigger identity.

Member names are PascalCase; the wire VALUES are the exact snake_case tokens
cross-repo consumers match on. Exarchos's TypeScript enum and Basileus's C#
enum round-trip against these by VALUE (INV-8 polyglot identity) — never by
ordinal.

Additive-evolution posture (DR-18): the set is CLOSED, but a future
budget-bounded trigger (the planned exploratory member, basileus PR #401
rec L-4) is admitted by APPENDING a member — a NON-BREAKING additive minor,
not a redesign (the ForkOccurrence payload carries an explicit schemaVersion
marker so this evolution is versioned, not implicit). Because emitted
converters stay strict, an added member is flagged NOTICE: consumers upgrade
before producers emit it. Removing or renaming a member is a breaking major.

GateClass.description:
Closed enum of the gate CLASSES a workflow's quality/merge gates evaluate
(#150, DR-1). This is the single typed gate identity shared across the
contract boundary so both runtimes consume ONE gate vocabulary.

Member names are PascalCase; the wire VALUES are the exact snake_case tokens
cross-repo consumers match on. Exarchos's TypeScript enum and Basileus's C#
enum round-trip against these **by value** (INV-8 polyglot identity) — never by
ordinal. Adding a class is an additive minor; renaming or removing one is a
breaking major.

class.description: The typed gate class this declaration evaluates (DR-1 — the shared gate identity).

id.description: Stable identifier for this gate declaration.

GateDeclaration.description:
A single gate declaration on a workflow (#150, DR-2): the typed gate CLASS it
evaluates, a stable id, and — ONLY when measured — its reliability telemetry.

`class` is the single typed gate identity (DR-1, GateClass) both runtimes
consume; it is non-optional. `reliability` is optional because it is stamped
from telemetry after the fact — a freshly-declared gate carries none, and no
authoring channel may supply it. Presence of the block is not the same as
`sampleSize ≥ 1`: a stamped block may report zero observations (see
GateReliability). When present, its `source` provenance is mandatory.

fpr.description: Measured false-positive rate of the gate, a fraction in the closed unit interval.

sampleSize.description:
Number of observations the measurement was computed over. Zero is valid:
the block is present (stamped) but no observations have been recorded yet.
Omitting the reliability block on GateDeclaration is the "never stamped"
state; do not treat `sampleSize: 0` as equivalent to absence.
Keep `@minValue(0)` (#156.1).

source.description:
Provenance of the measurement — where this reliability number came from.
REQUIRED: reliability is telemetry-measured, never hand-authored, so a
reliability block without a source is invalid.

GateReliability.description:
Measured-reliability telemetry for a gate (#150, DR-2).

This block is NEVER hand-authored: it is populated only from measured gate
telemetry, so `source` — the PROVENANCE of the measurement — is REQUIRED. A
reliability block that omits `source` is rejected at the schema boundary
(there is no anonymous, unattributable reliability number). The authoring
channel (the builder DSL / import) surfaces no reliability field at all, so
nothing on the write path can smuggle a value in; reliability is stamped only
from telemetry.

Presence of this block is the "stamped from telemetry" state. That is
distinct from GateDeclaration omitting `reliability` (never stamped). A
stamped block MAY report `sampleSize: 0` — measured, zero observations —
so `@minValue(0)` is the correct floor (#156.1). Tightening to
`@minValue(1)` would collapse those two states and is a constraint-narrow
on the shipped 0.7.0 contract; do not re-open it.

requiredEvidenceFields.description:
The evidence FIELD NAMES a future fork occurrence must carry for this trigger
(declaration side — NOT runtime values). Each is a plain string moniker
(INV-8): the name of a field on the occurrence's evidence (for example
`provisionalStampEventId`), never a CLR type. At least one field: a permitted
trigger that names no evidence declares no justification schema. Per-trigger
runtime completeness is enforced where occurrences are born — the generated
guard (DR-9) — never at authoring time; this shape pins the declared floor.

PermittedForkTrigger.description:
Wire-IR permitted fork trigger with its DECLARATION-side evidence-ref schema
(#151, DR-10 / DR-8). Pairs one closed ForkTrigger the workflow may fork on
with the NAMES of the evidence fields a future fork occurrence must carry to
justify that trigger.

This is the declaration half: field-NAME declarations, never runtime VALUES —
those exist only when a fork actually happens (see the occurrence side,
ForkOccurrence / ForkEvidence, in the Events family). Every entry is a plain
string moniker (INV-8): a field name, never a CLR type or a runtime payload.

useJitter.description: Whether to apply jitter to backoff.

RetryConfiguration.description:

SkillStep.description:
Skill step — a CLR step type implementing the skill protocol. `stepType` is
the **simple type name** moniker (LB-2): language-neutral, not assembly- or
namespace-qualified.

confidenceThreshold.description: Confidence threshold below which the low-confidence handler fires.

StepConfigurationDefinition.description:
Wire-IR step configuration tree (mirrors the builder's
`StepConfigurationDefinition`). All members are optional — an unconfigured
step omits the whole object.

StepDefinition.description:
Wire-IR step definition (issue #50): a discriminated union over the five step
kinds. Each arm pins its `kind` discriminator const and spreads the shared
`StepCommon` fields. This is the wire shape both consumers (Exarchos Zod,
Basileus) derive from.

StepRuntime.description:
Reserved runtime placement for a step (v3.3.0 federation forward-compat slot).
Optional on every step kind; absence means the default `exarchos`. No behavior
is attached in 0.2.0 — the slot exists so a future federation release is an
additive minor, not a breaking V2.

fromStepId.description: Step id this transition originates from.

isDefault.description: Whether this is the default (fallthrough) transition.

TransitionDefinition.description:
Wire-IR transition — a directed edge between two steps (mirrors the builder's
`TransitionDefinition`).

schemaId.description:
The `$id` of the schema describing this contract. An absolute URI, matching
the `$id` the emitter stamps on every emitted schema document.

TypedContractRefV1.description:
The kernel's `inputs` / `outputs: TypedContract` slot — FROZEN AS A SLOT,
not as a type system.

A step's accepted and returned CLR types are deliberately not projected
(LB-2): the wire carries simple-name monikers, never assembly-qualified
handles. Rather than invent a second type system on the wire, this slot
carries a reference to a schema that already has an identity — the `$id` of
a JSON Schema document.

The reference is never resolved by Strategos. Whether the id resolves, and
to what, is the resolving consumer's concern.

predicateExpression.description: Declarative predicate description (not executable code, LB-1).

errorMessage.description: Error message surfaced when validation fails.

ValidationDefinition.description:
Wire-IR validation definition (mirrors the builder's `ValidationDefinition`).
`predicateExpression` is a **declarative description** of the predicate, not
executable code (LB-1) — it is the same string the builder stores for
visualization / diagnostics.

id.description:
Stable identifier, when the statement has one (for example `U-1` from the
repository invariants catalog). Omitted for a free statement.

WorkflowAuthorityStatementV1.description:
The #193 kernel's `authority { … }` block and its typed-contract slot.

**Carried, not proved.** Strategos serializes every member below and checks
NONE of them in 3.0. No analyzer, no emitter and no runtime path reads this
block. It exists so the semantic plane has one vocabulary for the authority
frame from birth, rather than each consumer inventing its own and converging
later. A consumer that acts on this block acts on unproved data.One statement in the authority frame.

A statement is a model rather than a bare string on purpose. The frame's
members are unproved in 3.0, so the fields a proved statement will need
(a provenance ref, a check id, a severity) are not known yet. Adding a
field to this model later is additive. Replacing `string[]` with a model
later would be a narrowing, and a narrowing here would be the design error
#209 exists to avoid.

assumptions.description: What the workflow takes for granted about its environment.

delegatedDecisions.description: Decisions the workflow may make without escalating.

escalationBoundaries.description: The boundaries past which the workflow must escalate.

WorkflowAuthorityV1.description:
The authority frame of a workflow: what it must preserve, what it is for,
what it takes for granted, what it may decide alone, and where it must stop.

Every member is OPTIONAL, following the `InvariantEntry` v3 precedent, so a
definition that declares no frame omits the block entirely and a definition
that declares one member carries only that member.

schemaVersion.description:
Wire-IR schema version: pinned literal `1.0`. While the Contracts package
is pre-1.0 a minor may narrow this document in place and every narrowing
must be listed in `schemas/breaking-changes.allowlist.json`; after 1.0 a
breaking change requires a V2 root.

name.description: Workflow name (the IR identity, matches the builder's `WorkflowDefinition.Name`).

gates.description:
Gate declarations for this workflow (#150, DR-3). Consumer-plane data: the
generated saga does NOT consume gates — they flow through the shared wire IR
so both runtimes see the same gate vocabulary from birth. OPTIONAL and
additive; a workflow with no declared gates omits the slot entirely.

A GateStep may back-reference a declaration here by its `gateId`. That a
`gateId` must name an id present in this list is a semantic rule JSON Schema
cannot express (see README, "Dangling gateId"); the build-time import
front-end enforces it (DR-13/DR-15), not this schema.

diagnosticForks.description:
Diagnostic fork edges for this workflow (#151, DR-10). The DECLARATIVE half of
the fork/compensation edge (DR-7): where the workflow may fork, the closed
triggers permitted with their evidence-ref schema, the `maxForks` bound, and
the compensation seed. OPTIONAL and additive — a workflow with no fork edge
omits the slot entirely, so this is a NON-BREAKING wire change.

INV-8: every reference inside a DiagnosticForkDefinition is a string moniker,
never a CLR type. The generated saga lowers the edge (DR-9); the runtime
companion is ForkOccurrence (DR-8) in the Events family.

contentHash.description:
SHA-256 over this definition's STRUCTURAL fields, lowercase hex (#193
kernel `identity.contentHash`). Prose is excluded, on the same rules
`OntologyGraphHasher` already applies: documentation churn must not change
the hash, because the hash exists to say when the shape changed.

OPTIONAL and additive. A producer that does not stamp one omits the slot,
and no Strategos path requires it. #204 reads it for tamper and skew
detection across an assembly boundary.

authority.description:
The #193 kernel's authority frame — invariants, goals, assumptions,
delegated decisions and escalation boundaries (#193, DR-kernel).

**Carried, not proved in 3.0.** Strategos serializes this block and checks
none of it. See `WorkflowAuthorityV1`.

entryStepId.description: Step id of the workflow entry step, if set.

terminalStepId.description: Step id of the workflow terminal step, if set.

WorkflowDefinitionV1.description:
Wire-IR root for a serialized Strategos workflow (issue #50).

This is the **wire contract** — the flat, language-neutral document that
cross-product consumers (Exarchos Zod, Basileus, visualization, schema diff)
read. It is the export-only projection target of the in-memory builder IR
`WorkflowDefinition<TState>` (see `WorkflowDefinitionProjection.ToContract`):
the projection drops executable code (LB-1) and reduces CLR `System.Type`
handles to simple-name string monikers (LB-2).

`schemaVersion` is a pinned literal `1.0`. While the Contracts package is
pre-1.0 a minor may narrow this document in place, and every narrowing must
be listed in `schemas/breaking-changes.allowlist.json`; after 1.0 a breaking
change requires a V2 root.
